speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Manpower pertaining to the voluntary Safety Time-out focused on vehicular safety from 13 to 27 January 2026, what specific enforcement or inspection actions, if any, has the Ministry taken to ensure that companies not only pause operations but also implement concrete improvements to vehicular safety practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM and the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council, through its existing channels, have encouraged companies to participate in the Safety Time-out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They have also issued WSH advisories to guide companies on the key learning points from the recent incidents and the relevant safety practices to be reinforced with their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition to initiating the recent Safety Time-out, MOM conducts regular inspections in the high-risk sectors where vehicular hazards are present.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This ensures that companies comply with measures, such as having proper traffic management at the workplace and ensuring the drivers or operators have the requisite competencies.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The reality on the ground is that tight scheduling and shift work patterns continue to entrench workers' fatigue.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And we all know driving heavy vehicles is a very challenging task because of the vehicles' large size and unladen weight.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Fatigue therefore compounds this difficulty and increases safety risks.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can the Minister of State share whether there are further plans to manage drivers' fatigue?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I would also like to ask how many employers have tapped on the resources and grants available for companies to adopt vehicular safety technologies?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If these technologies are proven to improve safety, but take-up rate among these companies are low, then would the Ministry consider mandating the adoption of such technology to improve vehicular safety outcomes?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Perhaps we can start off with the higher risk sectors.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: And as tragic as it was, I could not see any common trends or any root causes, per se.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: These could potentially have happened due to unfortunate lapses of judgement or not adhering to the existing safety protocols.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: But that said, I would urge the Member to await the final investigations, which are currently ongoing, and then we can discuss on subsequent moves that need to be put in place, either be it because of fatigue or otherwise.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: But he has raised important points about fatigue affecting drivers and I wanted to just say that what we have in place are WSH guidelines on fatigue management, where rest breaks are recommended and the need to manage shift work as well, as part of these WSH guidelines.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: And in terms of technologies, we see some useful technologies, such as the driver status monitoring system, which detects driver fatigue.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: I think we have to continue to push the adoption of technologies, especially the proven ones.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: I think what we want to try to avoid is having a Maslow's Hammer type of a situation, where every problem is seen to be a nail that requires hammering.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: Instead, what we need to have is a repertoire of solutions, sometimes a loving nudge, a firm stare or a warning might in fact do the trick.

speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
text: Having said that, the ultimate aim is really to have a lasting and sustainable safety culture in Singapore, and I look forward to working with the Member on it.
